    //==
    // # The IGeoRegion containment tests
    //
    // Altitude is ignored throughout, as the interface says. The bounds and circle
    // tests are exact; the polygon test treats the rings as straight in
    // longitude/latitude, which is the usual convention for a GeoJSON-style
    // polygon and diverges from the geodesic edges the type's doc comment names
    // only for rings whose edges span a large fraction of the planet.
    // No ring test is antimeridian-aware: a ring whose longitudes wrap must be
    // split at the antimeridian first, which is the same requirement GeoJSON
    // places on its polygons.

    // Inside the latitude band and inside the longitude band. West greater than
    // East encodes a band crossing the antimeridian, so that case tests the
    // union of the two pieces rather than their (empty) intersection.
    ContainsCoordinate(self: GeoBounds, coordinate: GeoCoordinate): Boolean {
        var latitude = coordinate.Latitude.Radians;
        var longitude = coordinate.Longitude.Radians;
        var west = self.West.Radians;
        var east = self.East.Radians;
        var inBand = latitude >= self.South.Radians && latitude <= self.North.Radians;
        var inLongitudes = west <= east
            ? longitude >= west && longitude <= east
            : longitude >= west || longitude <= east;
        return inBand && inLongitudes;
    }
```

    // Inside the boundary ring and outside every hole.
    ContainsCoordinate(self: GeoPolygon, coordinate: GeoCoordinate): Boolean
        => self.Boundary.RingContainsCoordinate(coordinate)
           && self.Holes.All(hole => hole.RingContainsCoordinate(coordinate).Not);
```

    // Within the geodesic radius of the centre, measured on a sphere of mean
    // Earth radius.
    ContainsCoordinate(self: GeoCircle, coordinate: GeoCoordinate): Boolean
        => GreatCircleDistance(self.Center, coordinate, self.MeanEarthRadius).Meters
           <= self.Radius.Meters;
}
